name: Dholl puri
subtitle: Dholl puri is a Mauritian pancake made from ground yellow split peas seasoned with cumin and turmeric, cooked on a tawa (flat pan).

facts.label: Type of dish
facts.value: A pancake of ground yellow split peas seasoned with cumin and turmeric, griddled on a tawa (flat pan)

facts.label: Eaten with
facts.value: Wrapped around butter bean curry (cari gros pois), rougaille (spicy Creole tomato sauce), pickled vegetables, coriander chutney and chilli

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Introduced by Bhojpuri-speaking Indian indentured labourers from Bihar more than a century ago

facts.label: Festive form
facts.value: A giant dholl puri filled with fish, deer or goat meat is traditionally served at Hindu wedding feasts on a banana leaf; a vendor made a mini version in the 1960s and sold it door to door

facts.label: Origin (family account)
facts.value: A vendor family says its founder created it about a century ago by combining roti and tekwa (fried split-pea cakes), both brought by Indian immigrants

facts.label: Change
facts.value: Kidney beans as an accompaniment were introduced by vendor Ramesh Ramsahye Maraz as a substitute for mashed potato, and spread to other vendors

facts.label: Price in the past
facts.value: Once sold at 15 cents (rupee) a pair

parts.text: Dholl puri is a Mauritian pancake made from ground yellow split peas seasoned with cumin and turmeric, cooked on a tawa (flat pan). It is described as originating from Indian stuffed flatbreads brought to Mauritius by Bhojpuri-speaking indentured labourers from Bihar more than a century ago, and is now found all over the island.

It is wrapped around butter bean curry (cari gros pois), rougaille, pickled vegetables, coriander chutney and chilli; one vendor family says it added kidney beans as a filling, which other vendors adopted.

blocks.title: Dholl puri
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by SBS Food; the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: Resting time is given as 20–30 minutes. SBS notes that Australian tablespoons are 20 ml. Served warm wrapped around curries, achards and chutneys.

steps.text: Soak the split peas overnight (start a day ahead).
Dry-toast the cumin seeds in a pan and grind them in a mortar.
Drain and rinse the peas, then boil in fresh water until just tender.
Drain thoroughly and process the peas with the cumin to a powdery mixture; season with salt.
Mix the flour with the turmeric and two pinches of salt, add the water, bring together into a smooth dough and knead.
Cover with a damp cloth and let the dough rest.
Divide into balls of about 60 g, press a hollow into each, fill with the pea mixture and close the dough over it.
Roll each ball very thin on a floured surface.
Cook in an oiled pan over high heat, brushing the top with oil before turning; about 2 minutes per side.
